units.teacherOverview: Week 4 assesses mastery after Weeks 1–3. On Day 4 score independent work; Day 5 corrections and alternate items support reassessment. Never disclose this teacher-only guide in student/guardian responses.

lessons.preparation: Prepare accessible workspaces and independent scoring evidence for Day 1. Use original-equation checks, annotated misconceptions and individualized feedback.

workedAnswers.prompt: Independent 3: Explain why 5y+6 is not a solution.
workedAnswers.answer: It is an expression; a solution requires an equation and a value of y.

misconceptions: Combining unlike terms or losing a distributive negative changes an expression.
An inequality division by a negative requires reversing the comparison direction.
A contextual count may require a whole-number restriction even when the algebra gives a fraction.
interventions: Use color-coded like-term cards and a step/reason table; require an original-expression check.
For inequalities, test the boundary and one value on each side before accepting the solution set.
extensions: Compare two valid methods and justify which makes the problem structure easiest to see.
